Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Anshuman Singh Chauhan, learned Counsel for
applicant.
2. Mr. Bhaskar Chand Joshi, learned AGA for the State.
3. This Application has been filed for anticipatory bail in
FIR No.0463 of 2026 dated 16.09.2026, registered at Police
Station Rishikesh, District Dehradun under Sections 318(4),
336(3), 338, 340(2) and 61(2) of BNS, 2023.
4. Learned Counsel for applicant submits that applicant
is not named in the FIR; she works as a Clerk/Computer
Operator in M/s Rajdeep Enterprises; the allegations
levelled in FIR against the named accused are that they
were cheating people for providing them employment in
AIIMS under construction in Kichha, Distt. U.S. Nagar.
5. It is contended by learned Counsel for the applicant
that the applicant is 26 years' old girl who works as
computer operator/clerk with outsourcing agency M/s
Rajdeep Enterprises, and therefore, applicant, in good faith,
put signatures on the so-called appointment orders issued
by said agency; she has no connection with the crime; she
had just put signatures on appointment orders under the
directions of her employer/senior officer in the agency.

UKHC010187122026
2026:UHC:9553
6. Per contra, learned State Counsel submits that
applicant admits her signature in the alleged appointment
orders; the investigation is going on; and since the offences
disclosed in the FIR are very serious in nature, therefore,
applicant does not deserve any protection from this Court.
7. Having heard learned Counsel for the parties and
having perused the contents of the FIR as well as the
material placed on record, this Court is of the view that
applicant is a small-scale computer operator/clerk working
with the agency; it can be admitted prima facie at this stage
that signature, if any, put by applicant in appointment
orders were in exercise of her duties as employee of the
agency.
8. In such view of the matter, applicant deserves
anticipatory bail at this stage.
9. For the foregoing reasons, the present application,
filed for anticipatory bail, is allowed. It is directed that in
the event of arrest of the applicant-Saumya Singh, she shall
be released on anticipatory bail on executing a personal
bond of Rs. 30,000/- and two reliable sureties, each of the
like amount, to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer,
subject to the following conditions: -
(i) Applicant shall attend the trial court regularly and she
shall not seek any unnecessary adjournment;
(ii) Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any
inducement, threat or promise to any person, acquainted
with the facts of this case;
(iii) Applicant shall not leave the country without the
previous permission of the trial court.

8. It is clarified that if the applicant misuses or violates
any of the conditions, imposed upon her, the prosecution
agency will be free to move the Court for cancellation of the
anticipatory bail.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 16.10.2026 R.Dang
